final_answer: Turbine T-4 experienced its only significant failure when the bearing seal corroded through on 14 March 2025, allowing seawater into the nacelle; the root cause was traced to corrosion of the bearing seal housing. Over the full 24-month pilot, the site delivered 18.7 GWh to the grid, falling 6 percent short of the 19.9 GWh forecast. The project finished at EUR 41.25 million against an approved budget of EUR 36.7 million—an overrun of EUR 4.55 million (12.4 percent), mainly driven by the T-4 repair campaign. On the environmental front, an independent fish-monitoring programme found no statistically significant change in fish migration counts before and after installation (p = 0.41). Lead engineer Dr. Ines Marchetti recommended replacing the titanium fastener set with duplex stainless steel on all remaining nacelles to prevent recurrence, a recommendation the steering group accepted in principle. The steering groups decision was to approve Phase 2 for Q3 2026, contingent on completing the bearing seal redesign and passing a dry-dock endurance test.
